title: About — BetterMapandan.org
description: About the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan, and the Better Mapandan civic transparency project.
body: About About Better Mapandan An independent civic transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan. About Mapandan The municipality History Mapandan was created as an independent pueblo on December 28, 1887, through Director General No. 39. After a period of financial insolvency (1905–1908) when it was re-absorbed into Mangaldan, the town was re-established as an independent municipality in 1909 under Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants in the area. Geography Mapandan is a third-class municipality in the province of Pangasinan, Philippines. It covers a land area of 32.92 km² and is composed of 15 barangays. The municipality is located in the western part of Pangasinan, bordered by the Lingayen Gulf to the north and the Agno River floodplain to the south. Population 38,228 PSA Census 2020 Land Area 32.92 km² MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Barangays 15 DILG / Comelec History Mapandan through the years 1887–1909 From southern barrios of Mangaldan to an independent pueblo—and back again. Mapandan’s first two decades were defined by the courage of its founders, the fragility of a new town, and the determination to rise again. Read more Before 1887: Southern barrios of Mangaldan Before Mapandan existed as an independent pueblo, the area belonged to Mangaldan. The future municipality consisted of southern communities including Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The movement toward establishing a separate town was initiated by ten local leaders: Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, Andres Bongato, Ambrosio Calimlim, Valeriano Tamondong, Tomas Aquino, Fulgencio Nato, Filomeno Sarmiento, Jose Lalas, and Florencio Datuin. December 28, 1887: Mapandan becomes a pueblo Mapandan was established as an independent pueblo through Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, signed by Governor General Emilio Bravo. The new pueblo was initially composed of the southern barrios of Mangaldan: Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The first town center: Torres The first center of the new pueblo was in what is now Barangay Torres. The area had abundant pandan plants and was associated with a church where Fr. Jose Torres served as parish priest. However, the location proved inconvenient—too close to the southern boundary and too far from communities to the north. The center was eventually transferred to an area that had previously been a sitio of Apaya. Much of the land in the new Poblacion was owned by the Aquino family. Leon Hilario Aquino encouraged settlement by subdividing land into uniform lots and making them available to families. 1903: The epidemic An epidemic severely affected Mapandan, causing major population depletion, residents leaving the town, declining municipal resources, and a financial crisis. The 1903 census recorded Mapandan’s population at 4,198. 1905–1908: Return to Mangaldan Because of the population and financial problems caused by the epidemic, Mapandan was temporarily returned to its mother municipality, Mangaldan. 1909: Restoration Mapandan was formally re-established as a municipality under Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith. 1910s–1940s After its restoration, Mapandan developed as a predominantly agricultural community. Farming remained central to the local economy, with rice becoming the municipality’s principal crop. The decades ahead would bring war, occupation, and the beginning of reconstruction. Read more Agricultural foundations Rice became the municipality’s principal crop and livestock raising developed as an important secondary livelihood. The municipality’s current seal still reflects these agricultural foundations through its rice, cattle, chicken and hog imagery. 1940s: War, occupation and rebuilding The Second World War interrupted the development of communities across Pangasinan. In the postwar years, Mapandan’s communities entered a period of reconstruction and social and economic change. The decades following the war also brought changes in landholding, agriculture, education and local community organization. 1940s–1970s After the war, Mapandan’s communities began to take shape. New barangays were formed, land ownership changed hands, and the municipality entered a period of organized community development. Read more Barangays begin taking shape Instead of only telling municipal history, the history of how Mapandan’s communities formed tells an equally important story. Sta. Maria — Formerly part of Luyan, developed from former hacienda land. Tenants gained opportunities to own the land they had been farming after the war. It became a separate barrio in 1965. Golden — Formerly Amanoaoac North, a sitio of Amanoaoac. Its name was associated with the Golden Distillery, which operated after liberation. Golden became a separate barangay in 1967. Torres — The first seat of Mapandan, which once contained several sitios that later developed into separate barangays. 1967–1973: Community development Golden was officially approved as a separate barangay in 1967. The community then underwent substantial development including road improvement, waterworks, school construction, sports facilities, cooperative organization, agricultural training, and sanitation programs. 1972 — Golden was recognized as a SEATO/PACD Model Village, receiving a national-level award presented in Malacañang on September 8, 1972. 1972–1973 — Coral became a barangay through Municipal Council Resolution No. 87 (May 4, 1972), Provincial Board Resolution No. 155 (August 10, 1972), and Proclamation No. 11 (April 25, 1973), followed by a special election for barangay officials on May 6, 1973. 1980s–2001 Modernization Mapandan’s population grew substantially, its services expanded, and infrastructure developed. The municipality moved from historical survival toward economic growth. Read more Population growth Mapandan’s population grew steadily through the second half of the 20th century: 20,094 in 1980, 25,622 in 1990, and 30,775 in 2000. Infrastructure and services The municipality expanded roads, schools, health facilities, and public services. Community organizations grew alongside the population. 2002–2024 From a new municipal classification to healthcare expansion and digital government—Mapandan enters the 21st century with growing services, cultural pride, and a more connected community. Read more 2002: A new municipal classification Mapandan was elevated to a third-class municipality. The municipality credits then-Mayor Jose Ferdinand Z. Calimlim Jr. with spearheading income and revenue-generation strategies that contributed to the municipality’s elevation. 2010s: Celebrating the Pandan heritage The Pandan Festival developed into an important annual celebration of Mapandan’s identity, culture and community. The 9th Pandan Festival was held alongside the town fiesta from March 11–19, 2018. 2017–2018: Early digital government efforts The municipal government began developing an online presence that made government information, public notices, disaster information and community announcements accessible through the web. 2022–2024: Expanding healthcare access National health infrastructure funding supported the development of the Mapandan Super Health Center. The 2022 General Appropriations Act included ₱6.5 million for the project. Its first phase was inaugurated on March 15, 2024, expanding access to laboratory, dental and primary healthcare services for residents of Mapandan and nearby communities. 2020s: Government services go digital Mapandan’s government information infrastructure increasingly incorporates digital channels, including information and access guidance for the national eGovPH platform. 2024: Mapandan today More than 130 years after its establishment as a pueblo, Mapandan is a 15-barangay municipality with a population of 38,228. Its history has been shaped by migration, agriculture, community organization, local government, cultural traditions and continuing investment in public services. ← 1 / 5 → Source: Mayor Karl Vega, “History of Mapandan” — YouTube Population Growth Mapandan through the census Population by census year Year Population 1903 4,198 1918 6,049 1939 7,286 1948 9,836 1960 13,065 1970 16,653 1980 20,094 1990 25,622 2000 30,775 2010 34,077 2020 38,058 2024 38,228 Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, Census of Population (1903–2024) About the Project What is Better Mapandan? Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities. Our Mission To make government information accessible, understandable, and actionable for every Mapandan resident. We believe that open data strengthens democracy and empowers communities to participate meaningfully in local governance. How It Works We compile publicly available government data — from COA audit reports, PSA census data, municipal disclosures, and provincial issuances — into a single, easy-to-navigate website. Every piece of information is sourced and attributed. Open Source The source code is publicly available. Developers can contribute, audit, and improve the platform. View on GitHub → Independent Better Mapandan is not an official government website. It is a community-run project that operates independently of the Local Government Unit. Volunteer-Run Built and maintained entirely by volunteers. No government funding is used. Cost to the people of Mapandan: ₱0. Contribute Get involved Better Mapandan thrives on community participation. Here's how you can help: Report Incorrect Information Spotted an error? Help us keep the data accurate by reporting mistakes. Report an error → Contribute Code Developers can contribute features, fix bugs, or improve accessibility on GitHub. Fork on GitHub → Verify Data Help verify government information by cross-referencing with official sources. Submit verification → Share with Residents Spread the word about Better Mapandan so more residents can access government information. Disclaimer Important notice Better Mapandan is an independent community project and is not an official website of the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. Information presented on this site is compiled from publicly available government sources and community research. While we strive for accuracy, we cannot guarantee the completeness or timeliness of all data. For official government information, please visit mapandan.gov.ph or contact the municipal government directly.

title: BetterMapandan.org — Mapandan, Pangasinan Transparency Portal
description: An independent, citizen-run transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan — officials, budget, ordinances, services, and emergency contacts, built under the BetterGov.ph BetterLGU initiative.
body: Independent · Citizen-Maintained · Pangasinan Mapandan, in the open. Officials, budgets, ordinances, and frontline services for the Municipality of Mapandan — gathered from public records and kept in one place, so every resident can find what their local government is doing. Browse Services See the Budget Find a Service Search every service Mapandan offers — by what you're trying to do, not which office handles it. Popular: business permit local hospital barangay clearance tax declaration Services Budget Legislation Hotlines 38,228 Official Source: PSA Census 2020 Residents 15 Official Source: DILG / Comelec Barangays 10,685 Official Source: RHU Mapandan 2023 Households 1,161.24/km² Official Computed: 38,228 ÷ 32.92 km² Pop. density 32.92² Official Source: MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Land area Third-Class Municipality · Region I A rice-growing town in Pangasinan's third district Mapandan sits in the Third Congressional District of Pangasinan, bounded by San Jacinto to the north, Mangaldan to the northwest, Manaoag to the east, and Santa Barbara to the south. Covering 30.00 square kilometres, around three-quarters of its land supports agriculture — mainly rice, alongside corn, livestock, and seasonal vegetables. The municipal administration operates under the tagline “Kaakibat niyo ang Aktibo at Responsableng Liderato” (Partnering with you in Active and Responsible Leadership). 01 Founded Dec. 28, 1887 Separated from Mangaldan as an independent pueblo under Governor General Emilio Bravo, led by ten local leaders including Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, and Andres Bongato. 02 Re-established 1909 A severe epidemic forced temporary re-annexation to Mangaldan. Full autonomy was restored via Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. 03 Agricultural heart Approximately 75% of the municipality's 30 km² is dedicated to lowland crop production, livestock, and poultry farming. A Brief History The Story of Mapandan From a new pueblo to a growing community Before 1887 Indigenous Roots The area belonged to Mangaldan as southern barrios — Payapay, Baloling, Apaya, and Amanoaoac — named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants along the Agno River floodplain. Dec. 28, 1887 Founding as a Pueblo Established as an independent municipality through Director General No. 39, led by ten local leaders including Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, and Andres Bongato. 1905–1909 Survival & Rebirth A severe epidemic forced temporary re-annexation to Mangaldan due to financial insolvency. Full autonomy was restored in 1909 under Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. 2020s Modern Mapandan A 15-barangay municipality of 38,228 residents, investing in the Super Health Center, Pandan Festival, and infrastructure growth. Read the full history & explore historical photos → Stories Behind Our Barangays 15 communities, 15 histories Each of Mapandan's barangays has its own story of origin, growth, and community life. Sources & Historical Notes Much of Mapandan's historical material comes from the Municipality of Mapandan's official website, including the Municipal Profile, Physical Characteristics, and individual barangay history pages. Population data is from the Philippine Statistics Authority. Development milestones reference the Philippine News Agency and Department of Budget and Management records. title: Accessibility Statement — BetterMapandan.org
description: Accessibility commitment and standards for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Support Accessibility Statement Our commitment to making government information accessible to all residents. Our commitment Better Mapandan is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We continually improve the user experience for everyone and apply the relevant accessibility standards. Conformance Status We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at the AA level. These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible for people with disabilities. Measures Taken We have implemented the following accessibility features across the site: Semantic HTML structure Skip-to-content navigation link Visible focus indicators Sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum) Keyboard-accessible navigation Screen-reader-friendly labels Descriptive link text Proper heading hierarchy Accessibility features Keyboard Navigation All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard. Use Tab to move between elements, Enter to activate links and buttons, and Escape to close overlays. Screen Readers The site uses semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and proper heading hierarchy to ensure screen readers can navigate the content effectively. Color & Contrast All text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Information is never conveyed through color alone — icons, labels, and text are always provided alongside color coding. Text Resizing The site uses relative units (rem, em) for text sizing. Users can resize text up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. Forms All form inputs are associated with labels. Error messages are descriptive and programmatically associated with the relevant input fields. Tables Data tables include proper header associations ( <th scope> ), captions where appropriate, and are responsive on mobile devices. Known limitations We are aware of the following accessibility limitations and are working to address them: PDF documents: Some linked government documents (COA reports, provincial issuances) may not be fully accessible. We provide HTML summaries where possible. Interactive maps: The Leaflet map is navigable via keyboard but may present challenges for screen reader users. We provide alternative text descriptions and a data table fallback. Third-party content: Embedded content from external government websites may not meet the same accessibility standards. Feedback We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of Better Mapandan. If you encounter accessibility barriers, please let us know: Report an Issue Use our reporting form to describe the accessibility issue, the page URL, and your browser/device information. Report accessibility issue → GitHub Issues Developers can file accessibility issues directly on our GitHub repository. Open GitHub issue →

title: Frequently Asked Questions — BetterMapandan.org
description: Common questions about government services, documents, and civic information for Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Support Frequently Asked Questions Answers to common questions about government services and civic information in Mapandan. General About Better Mapandan Is this an official government website? No. Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. For official information, visit mapandan.gov.ph . How is this project funded? Better Mapandan is entirely volunteer-run and uses no government funding. The cost to the people of Mapandan is ₱0. Hosting and domain costs are covered by the BetterGov.ph initiative. Where does the data come from? All data is compiled from publicly available government sources: COA audit reports, PSA census data, DILG disclosures, BLGF treasury data, provincial issuances, and municipal announcements. Every source is attributed on the page where the data appears. How do I report incorrect information? Visit our Report Incorrect Information page. Provide the page URL, the specific error, and the correct information if known. Our volunteers will review and update the data. Services Government services How do I get a birth certificate? Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) at the 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion. Bring a valid ID and the required fee. Processing time is typically 3–5 working days. See the full requirements on the Birth Certificate service page . How do I apply for a business permit? Visit the Municipal Treasurer's Office (MTO) with your DTI/SEC registration, barangay clearance, and other required documents. New permits are processed in 3–5 working days. See the Business Permit service page for full details. How do I get a building permit? Apply through the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO). Building permits require a zoning clearance, architectural plans, and structural plans. Processing takes 10–15 working days. See the Building Permit service page . How do I request a barangay clearance? Visit your barangay hall with a valid ID. Barangay clearances are typically issued the same day. This is often a prerequisite for other government transactions. Data & Transparency Data questions What does "Placeholder" mean on data? Some data is marked as "Placeholder" when the exact figure is not yet available from official sources. We use reasonable estimates based on available data and clearly mark these so residents know the difference between verified and estimated figures. How often is the data updated? Each data section includes a "Last updated" timestamp. Major updates happen when new COA audit reports, PSA census data, or municipal financial disclosures become available. The site is continuously improved by volunteers. Can I download the data? Yes. The Statistics page includes CSV download options for chart data. The Transparency page provides links to source documents. All data is publicly available and free to reuse under open data principles. How can I verify the data myself? Every data section includes a source attribution and, where available, a link to the original document. You can cross-reference with official sources like the COA website, PSA, or the municipal government directly. Contact Still have questions? For government services Contact the relevant office directly. See the Government Directory for phone numbers and email addresses. For this website Report issues, suggest improvements, or contribute on GitHub . For data corrections, use the Report Incorrect Information form.

title: Privacy Policy — BetterMapandan.org
description: Privacy policy for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Legal Privacy Policy How we handle data on the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal. Overview Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. We collect minimal data and are committed to protecting your privacy. Information We Collect Automatically collected: When you visit Better Mapandan, our hosting provider (GitHub Pages) may collect standard web server logs including your IP address, browser type, referring URL, and pages visited. This is standard server operation and is not used to identify individual visitors. Search queries: The search functionality runs entirely in your browser. Your search queries are never sent to a server or stored. Language preference: If you use the language switcher (when available), your preference is stored locally in your browser and is never transmitted to us. How We Use Information We do not use, sell, or share personal information. Server logs are used only for maintaining the website and understanding usage patterns in aggregate. Cookies Better Mapandan does not use cookies. The language preference is stored using localStorage , which is a browser-only storage mechanism and is not transmitted to any server. Third-Party Services The site loads the following external resources: Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) — for font loading Open-Meteo API (open-meteo.com) — for weather data (loaded only on the homepage) Leaflet / OpenStreetMap — for the interactive map (loaded only on the homepage) These services have their own privacy policies. We do not share any personal data with them. Data Sources All government data presented on this site is compiled from publicly available official sources. This data is already public and is presented here for informational purposes. Changes to This Policy This privacy policy may be updated from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. Contact For privacy-related inquiries, please open an issue on our GitHub repository or use the report form .

title: Agriculture Subsidy
body: Description The Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) provides various government-subsidized agricultural programs to support local farmers and fisherfolk in Mapandan. These programs include subsidies for seeds, fertilizers, farm equipment, and technical assistance to improve agricultural productivity and livelihood. Availability of subsidies depends on national and provincial funding allocations. Requirements Farmer registration with the Municipal Agriculture Office Barangay certification of residency and farming activity Farm location and land area information Procedure Register with the Municipal Agriculture Office (MAO) as a farmer or fisherfolk. Secure a barangay certification confirming your farming activity and residency. Submit your registration and requirements to the MAO. Wait for availability announcement of agricultural subsidies or programs. Receive agricultural assistance or subsidies upon program approval. title: Aics
body: Description Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations (AICS) is a government program that provides financial assistance to individuals and families facing emergencies such as medical crises, bereavement, or other unforeseen circumstances. In Mapandan, AICS assistance is administered by the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD). Requirements Barangay certification stating the resident’s crisis situation Medical certificate (for medical-related assistance) Death certificate (for burial assistance) Valid government-issued ID Case study or social worker assessment Procedure Secure a barangay certification from your barangay captain or kagawad. Gather all required documents (medical certificate, death certificate, etc.). Visit the MSWDO office and submit your application with supporting documents. Wait for the social worker’s assessment and case study. Receive financial assistance upon approval of your application. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSWDO) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 1–3 working days Fee: Free Where to Apply: MSWDO Office, Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1751 / 0930-641-3934 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Birth Certificate
body: Description A birth certificate is a vital record that serves as proof of identity, age, and Filipino citizenship. The Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) of Mapandan issues certified copies of locally registered birth certificates. This document is required for school enrollment, passport application, employment, and other legal purposes. Requirements Valid government-issued ID of the requesting party PSA copy of the birth certificate (if available, for verification) Barangay certification of residency (for the person named on the certificate) Affidavit of two disinterested persons (required for delayed registration only) Procedure Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office and present valid identification. Fill out the request form and provide the necessary supporting documents. Pay the certification fee at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the certified birth certificate upon release. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 10 minutes (standard) to 10+ days (late registration) Fee: ₱115 (standard) / ₱215 (unmarried) / ₱100 (hospital) / ₱315–₱1,015 (late registration) Where to Apply: Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Building Permit
body: Description A building permit is a legal requirement under the National Building Code of the Philippines (PD 1096) for any construction, renovation, alteration, or demolition of a building or structure. The Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) of Mapandan reviews and issues building permits after ensuring compliance with safety standards, zoning, and structural requirements. Requirements Plans duly signed & sealed by licensed professionals Certified true copy of Tax Declaration (from Assessor Office) Xerox copy of land title (from Register of Deeds) Community Tax Certificate (from Treasury Office) Latest Tax receipts (from Treasury Office) Electrical & Sanitary permit (from Municipal Health Office) Confirmation of adjoining lot owners Certification from Barangay Captain Application for locational clearance (from Zoning Office) 2 Affidavits (from Notary Public) Affidavit of consent if not lot owner (from Notary Public) Fire Safety clearance (from BFP Office) Affidavit of adjoining lot owners Procedure Obtain a zoning clearance from the MPDC / Zoning Office. Prepare architectural and structural plans signed by licensed professionals. Submit all documents to the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) for review. Pay the building permit fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Receive the approved building permit after technical evaluation. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Engineering Office (MEO) Classification: Highly Technical Mode: in-person Processing Time: 3 working days (Simple) / 7 working days (Complex) / 20 working days (Highly Technical) per RA 11032 Fee: Based on project cost (schedule per National Building Code) Where to Apply: Municipal Engineering Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Business Permit
body: Description A business permit is required for all individuals or entities intending to operate a commercial business within the Municipality of Mapandan. This permit is issued after compliance with documentary and safety requirements and upon payment of applicable fees. Requirements Filled up UNIFIED Form / Community Tax Certificate (from BPLO/Treasury Office) DTI/SEC/CDA Registration (from DTI/SEC/CDA Office or Online Application) BIR COR, if available (from RDO Calasiao) Barangay Clearance (System Integrated) Procedure Fill up the UNIFIED form and submit necessary requirements for verification (10 min). BPLO encodes data into the e-BPLS System. BPLO endorses applicant to various offices: Engineering (Occupancy Certificate), MPDC (Zoning Certificate), RHU (Health Certificate & Sanitary Permit), BFP (Fire Safety Inspection Certificate) (44 min). Pay fees and charges at the Treasury Office. Proceed to the Mayor's Office for issuance of Business Permit. Claim business plate and sticker at the Treasury Office (10 min). title: Business Renewal
body: Description Businesses operating within Mapandan are required to renew their business permits annually. Renewal ensures that your business remains compliant with local regulations and avoids penalties for late filing. Requirements Filled up UNIFIED Form / Community Tax Certificate (from BPLO/Treasury Office) DTI/SEC/CDA Registration (from DTI/SEC/CDA Office or Online Application) BIR COR (from RDO Calasiao) Barangay Clearance (System Integrated) Procedure Fill up the UNIFIED form and submit necessary requirements for verification (10 min). BPLO encodes data into the e-BPLS System. BPLO endorses applicant to Engineering, MPDC, RHU, and BFP for required certificates (44 min). Pay fees at the Treasury Office. Fees include Mayor's Permit, Business Tax (% of Gross Sales), Plate & Sticker, Weights & Measure, Storage Fee, and Garbage Fee. Proceed to the Mayor's Office for issuance of renewed Business Permit. Claim business plate and sticker at the Treasury Office. Service Details Responsible Office: Business Permit and Licensing Office (BPLO) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: ~1 hour (similar to new business permit process) Fee: Mayor's Permit (₱500–₱1,000) + Business Tax (% of Gross Sales) + Business Plate & Sticker (₱250) + Weights & Measure (₱100–200) + Storage Fee (₱550) + Garbage Fee (₱800–₱1,200) Where to Apply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Cedula
body: Description The Community Tax Certificate (cedula) is computed as follows: Individual — ₱5.00 basic + ₱1.00 for every ₱1,000 gross income from business, profession, or property, but in no case shall exceed ₱5,000.00. Juridical — ₱500.00 basic + ₱2.00 for every ₱5,000 gross income from business or worth of real property, but in no case shall exceed ₱10,000.00. Interest of 24% per annum shall be imposed on individual or juridical securing their CTC from March 1 up to the end of the year. Requirements Old Community Tax Certificate (if available) Proof of income (if available) Procedure Go to Counters 1 and 2 and fill up the basic data form (15 min). Pay the required fees (3 min). Receive community tax certificate. Staff records in general collection system (2 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Treasury Office (MTO) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 20 minutes (15 min form filling + 3 min payment + 2 min recording) Fee: Individual: ₱5 + ₱1/₱1k income (max ₱5,000); Juridical: ₱500 + ₱2/₱5k income (max ₱10,000); 24% interest from March 1 Where to Apply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Health Consultation
body: Description The Municipal Health Office (MHO) / Rural Health Unit (RHU) provides free health consultation services to all residents of Mapandan. This includes general medical consultations, health advice, and referrals to higher-level health facilities when necessary. Walk-in patients are served on a first-come, first-served basis. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Procedure Register in Electronic Medical Record (EMR). Midwife registers new patients and encodes data. title: Land Transfer
body: Description Transfer of land ownership is the legal process of transferring property rights from one owner to another. The Municipal Assessor's Office (MASSO) records the transfer and updates the Tax Declaration under the new owner's name. The client first secures a tax clearance from the Treasury Office, then submits the transfer documents to the Assessor's Office. The Assessor records the transaction, cancels the old Tax Declaration, and issues a new one. Fee: ₱150 for recording. Requirements Deed of Sale, Deed of Donation, or other proof of transfer Tax Clearance from the Municipal Treasurer's Office Certified True Copy of Tax Declaration (from Assessor's Office) Valid Government-issued ID of the new owner BIR Certificate of Registration (if applicable) Procedure Secure a Tax Clearance from the Municipal Treasurer's Office. Obtain a Certified True Copy of the Tax Declaration from the Assessor's Office. Submit all required documents to the Assessor's Office. Assessor reviews and records the transfer (15 min). Assessor cancels the old Tax Declaration and prepares the new one (10 min). Pay ₱150 recording fee at the Treasury Office. Claim the new Tax Declaration under the new owner's name (5 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Assessor's Office (MASSO) Classification: Complex Mode: in-person Processing Time: 30 minutes (Assessor recording); full transfer may take 15–30 working days Fee: ₱150 (recording fee at Assessor's Office) Where to Apply: Municipal Assessor's Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Marriage License
body: Description A marriage license is a legal requirement before a marriage can be solemnized in the Philippines. The Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) of Mapandan processes marriage license applications, which include a required publication period. The license is valid for 120 days from the date of issuance. Requirements Municipal Form No. 90 Community Tax Certificate (cedula) Parental Consent of father/guardian (from MCR) Certificate of Family Planning (from Mun Health Office) Certificate of Pre-Marriage Counselling (from MSWD Office) CENOMAR / Birth Certificate (from PSA) Legal Capacity (from DFA, if one party is a foreigner) Procedure Both parties appear at the MCR and submit all required documents. Fill out the marriage license application form. Pay the applicable fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Wait for the 10-day publication period. After publication, claim the marriage license from the MCR. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 10–15 working days (including 10-day publication period) Fee: ₱862 Where to Apply: Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Name Correction
body: Description Republic Act No. 9048 authorizes the city or municipal civil registrar to correct clerical or typographical errors in civil registry entries without the need for a judicial order. This covers corrections in first names, nicknames, or minor spelling errors. This process does not apply to changes in gender, date of birth, or other substantive entries. Requirements Proof of Publication (from PSA) Certificate of Live Birth (from PSA) NBI Clearance Police Clearance (from PNP) Certificate of Employment (if employed) / Affidavit of non-employment Marriage Certificate, Medical records, SSS records, land title, baptismal certificate Procedure Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office and submit all required documents. File the petition for correction of clerical error. Pay the required fees at the Municipal Treasurer’s Office. Wait for the publication period to be completed. After publication and verification, claim the corrected birth certificate from the MCR. Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) Classification: Complex Mode: in-person Processing Time: 10-day posting + 5 days MCR decision + 2–3 months PSA processing Fee: ₱3,000 (change of first name) / ₱1,000 (correction of clerical error) Where to Apply: Municipal Civil Registrar’s Office, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Rpt Payment
body: Description Real property tax (RPT) is an annual tax on the assessed value of land, buildings, and improvements within Mapandan. Computation: Basic Tax = 1% of Assessed Value + Special Education Tax (SEF) = 1% of Assessed Value. Discounts: 10% for prompt payment, 20% for advance payment. Interest on unpaid real property tax: 2% per month but not to exceed 72%. Payment is processed at Counters 4-9 of the Treasury Office. Requirements Real Property Tax bill (from Assessor's Office) Previous Tax receipt (if available) Procedure Go to Counters 4 to 9 and request computation of real property tax. Staff computes the real property tax due (20 min). Pay the required fees (5 min). Receive the official receipt. Staff records in general collection system (5 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Municipal Treasury Office (MTO) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 30 minutes (20 min computation + 5 min payment + 5 min recording) Fee: Basic Tax (1% of AV) + SEF (1% of AV); 10% prompt payment discount; 20% advance payment discount Where to Apply: 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion Contact: (075) 696-0831 / 0998-577-3164 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter / Provincial Ordinance No. 253-2020 Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Sanitary Permit
body: Description A sanitary permit is required for all businesses that handle food, beverages, or other consumable products to ensure compliance with health and sanitation standards. The permit is issued by the Municipal Health Office (MHO) after an inspection of the business premises to verify that health and safety regulations are met. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Laboratory Tests: CBC, urinalysis, fecalysis, sputum exam, Hepatitis B (from RHU Primary Laboratory) Chest X-Ray, PA (from government or private diagnostic facility) Procedure Present official receipt from the Treasury Office. Laboratory examination of urine, feces, sputum is conducted by Medical Technologist (30 min). Refer to other laboratories for X-ray if needed (2 min). Refer result to MHO for interpretation (10 min). MHO does physical examination and interprets result (5 min). MHO prescribes medicines if needed (2 min). MHO signs the certification (2 min). List down certificate number on logbook and release certification (2 min). Service Details Responsible Office: Rural Health Unit (RHU) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 53 minutes per client Fee: ₱130 (laboratory tests) Where to Apply: Municipal Health Office, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen’s Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Senior Pwd Id
body: Description The Senior Citizen ID and Persons with Disabilities (PWD) ID are government-issued identification cards that provide holders with benefits and privileges under the law. Senior Citizens (60 years old and above) and PWDs are entitled to discounts, tax exemptions, and other benefits as mandated by RA 9994 (Senior Citizens Act) and RA 7277 (Magna Carta for Disabled Persons). The IDs are processed through the MSWDO and MCR in coordination with the national implementing agencies. Requirements Birth certificate or PSA-issued document as proof of age (for Senior Citizens) Barangay certification of residency Two (2) pieces of 2x2 ID photos Medical certificate (for PWD applicants, indicating the nature of disability) Procedure Secure a barangay certification of residency from your barangay office. For PWD applicants, obtain a medical certificate indicating the nature and severity of the disability. Submit all required documents to the MSWDO or MCR office. Wait for verification and processing of your application. Receive your Senior Citizen or PWD ID upon approval. title: Tax Declaration
body: Description A tax declaration is an official document that shows the assessed value of your real property for taxation purposes. The Municipal Assessor's Office (MASSO) of Mapandan issues certified true copies of Tax Declarations upon request. This document is required for property sales, loans, insurance applications, tax payments, and other legal transactions. The client submits a written request with property details and the Assessor's Office locates the record, prepares the certified true copy, and releases it upon payment. Requirements Written request stating the property location (lot number, block, street, barangay) Valid Government-issued ID Procedure Submit a written request with property details and valid ID to the Assessor's Office. Staff receives and verifies the request (5 min). Staff locates the Tax Declaration in the records (5 min). Staff prepares the certified true copy and stamps it (3 min). Pay ₱100 at the Treasury Office and claim the document (2 min). title: Marriage Counseling
body: Description The MSWDO provides pre-marriage counseling to would-be couples as required before obtaining a marriage license. The counseling covers family planning, rights and responsibilities of marriage, and strengthening family solidarity. The service is mandated by law and the certificate issued is a prerequisite for marriage license application. Would-be couples, couples with marital problems, couples of reproductive age, and solo parents may avail of this service. Requirements Personal Data Form Marriage Counselling Services Form Procedure Apply at the MSWDO. Staff will refer you to the Population Office. title: Disaster Relief
body: Description The MSWDO provides disaster relief assistance and rehabilitation services to families affected by floods, typhoons, fires, and other calamities. The service includes verification of affected families, distribution of relief goods through the Barangay Captain with the BDCC, and financial assistance (ESA) for families whose houses are totally destroyed. The MSWDO coordinates with the LGU, PSWDO, and DSWD Field Office I. Requirements Master list of affected families (from Barangay Captain) Barangay certificate Certificate of Indigency Procedure Report to the Barangay Captain the extent of damage. The Captain validates and forwards the list to MSWDO. MSWDO attends MDDC meeting conducted by the Local Chief Executive. MSWDO receives list of affected families and endorses to concerned social worker. Verification and inspection team (with Engineering, PNP, DSWD) assesses the damage. MSWDO requests and lobbies for allocation of relief goods from LGU, PSWDO, DSWD FO1. Distribution of relief goods through the Barangay Captain with the BDCC. For totally destroyed houses, MSWDO prepares project proposal for ESA funding. Financial assistance (ESA) is distributed to qualified beneficiaries. MSWDO monitors and evaluates project implementation for house repair/reconstruction. title: Pre Natal
body: Description The RHU provides pre-natal consultation services for antenatal women. The service includes registration in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR), OB history, vital signs, Leopold's maneuver, fetal heartbeat assessment, and fundic height measurement. Routine laboratory tests (CBC, urinalysis, HBsAg, RPR) are requested. The MHO conducts complete physical examination, interprets laboratory results, and provides health teaching on proper nutrition, prenatal care, breastfeeding, and immunization. High-risk patients are referred to higher-level facilities. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Medical Records, Laboratory Results, Prescription for Medicines (from previous physician, if any) Procedure Register in the Electronic Medical Record (EMR). Midwife encodes OB history, vital signs, and performs Leopold's maneuver. Request for routine laboratory tests (CBC, urinalysis, HBsAg Screening, RPR test). MHO performs complete physical examination and interprets laboratory results. If high-risk, patient is referred to a higher level of facility. Health teaching on proper nutrition, prenatal care, breastfeeding, and immunization. Service Details Responsible Office: Rural Health Unit (RHU) Classification: Simple Mode: in-person Processing Time: 55 minutes per client Fee: Free Where to Apply: Rural Health Unit, Poblacion Contact: (075) 632-1874 Source: Mapandan Citizen's Charter Last Updated: August 2025 Report incorrect information Scanned Document Scanned page from the official Mapandan Citizen's Charter listing the requirements, fees, processing time, and responsible staff for the service. title: Tb Dots
body: Description The RHU provides Directly Observed Treatment Short Course (TB DOTS) for patients with tuberculosis. The service includes registration, sputum examination, GeneXpert/TBDC testing, physical examination, and provision of anti-TB drugs with proper intake instructions. The MHO maintains patient confidentiality and monitors treatment compliance. Requirements Valid ID (government issued, employment, school, barangay certification) Medical Records, Prescription of Medicines (from previous physician, if any) Chest X-Ray PA Result (from government or private diagnostic facility) Procedure Register in the log book. Midwife encodes data, vital signs, and asks about symptoms and duration. Submit sputum for examination. Sputum examination is conducted. Patient is referred to GeneXpert/TBDC for further testing. title: Nutrition Immunization
body: Description The RHU implements the Nutrition Program for malnourished children (0–59 months and older) and the National Immunization Program (NIP) for children against vaccine-preventable diseases. The nutrition program includes assessment, deworming, feeding with nutrient-dense food, and monthly monitoring. The immunization program administers age-appropriate vaccines after reviewing the child's records and checking vital signs. Requirements Birth Certificate (Municipal Civil Registry) Medical Records, Vaccination Records (from hospital of birth or pediatrician) Procedure For malnourished children (0–59 months): Barangay Nutrition Scholar assesses weight and height. Physician refers to RHU for deworming and medical intervention. Child is fed with nutrient-dense food (high carbohydrate and protein). Monthly monitoring of weight, height, and alertness. For immunization: BHW interviews child's information and reviews records. Midwife checks vital signs (weight and temperature). Midwife administers age-appropriate vaccine. Midwife advises parent on child care and expected outcome. Schedule next vaccination. title: Electrical Zoning
body: Description A zoning clearance is required for electrical permits. The MPDC/Zoning Office evaluates the application, conducts land use assessment, and issues the Zoning Compliance Certificate for electrical installations. The process includes site evaluation/inspection, computation of fees, and approval by the Zoning Officer. Requirements Application for Zoning Permit (from MPDC) Accomplished Individual Assessment for Application of Temporary Housing Unit Form Tax Declaration of lot (from Assessor Office) Current Tax receipts (from Treasury Office) Affidavit of consent of lot owner Site development sketch indicating the ROW Affidavit of consent for Right of Way (from lot owner) Certification from Barangay Captain Procedure Inquire at the MPDC office and secure the application form. MPDC staff conducts interview and provides forms. Accomplish forms and prepare all required documents. MPDC checks and evaluates forms and required documents. Request for site evaluation/inspection. Land use assessment conducted. Go to Zoning office for computation of fees and charges. Pay fees at the Treasury Office. Present receipts to MPDC. Submit one photocopy of all forms and documents. MPDC prepares and submits documents. Zoning Officer approves application. Client signs logbook. title: Seed Certification

Requirements Membership in Seed Grower Association Actual harvest date notification to Seeds Inspector Procedure Submit/show requirements and inform the Seeds Inspector of the actual date of harvest. title: Birth Registration
body: Description Registration of birth at the Municipal Civil Registrar. Covers three pathways: (1) Attending midwife/hilot reports child's birth — requires Marriage Certificate of parents and Mun. Form 102; (2) Unmarried parents — requires Community Tax Certificate; (3) Hospital administrator — requires Accomplished Mun. Form 102. Late registration requires negative PSA certification and supporting documents. Fees: Misc Fee ₱115 (standard), ₱215 (unmarried), ₱100 (hospital), ₱315–₱1,015 (late registration depending on age). Requirements Marriage Certificate of parents from PSA (for attending midwife/hilot registration) Community Tax Certificate from Treasury Office (for unmarried parents) Accomplished Mun. Form 102 from MCR (for hospital registration) Negative certification from PSA (for late registration) Affidavit of delayed registration (for late registration) Supporting evidence: Baptismal Certificate, School records, ITR, Insurance Policy, Medical records, Barangay certification (for late registration) Procedure Attending midwife/hilot reports child's birth. MCR evaluates information and registers (10 min). For unmarried parents: Hospital admin or representative prepares documents (15 min). For late registration: Apply at MCR, verify from CRIS/Registry Book. If negative, submit requirements. Data typed in Certificate of Live Birth (15 min typing). MCR approves registration (after 10 days of posting for late registration). Secure copy of birth certificate. MCR releases documents (3 min). title: Ldrrmo Rescue Operation

title: Assessor True Copy
body: Description The Municipal Assessor's Office issues certified true copies of Tax Declarations upon request. The Tax Declaration is an official document showing the assessed value of real property for taxation purposes. The client submits a written request with the property details. The Assessor's Office locates the record, prepares the certified true copy, and releases it upon payment. Requirements Written request stating the property location (lot number, block, street, barangay) Valid Government-issued ID Procedure Submit a written request with property details and valid ID to the Assessor's Office. title: Legislative
body: Framework Local governance & statutory origins Legal Basis The Municipality of Mapandan operates under Republic Act No. 7160 (Local Government Code of 1991), situated within the Third Congressional District of Pangasinan. The Sangguniang Bayan — a unicameral local legislative council — exercises municipal legislative power, presided by the Municipal Vice Mayor and composed of elected councilors alongside ex-officio representatives from the Liga ng mga Barangay and the Sangguniang Kabataan Federation. Historical Origins Originally an agricultural barrio of Mangaldan referred to as balon baley ("new town"), Mapandan was first established as an independent pueblo pursuant to Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, promulgated by Governor General Emilio Bravo on December 28, 1887. Following population and fiscal losses caused by an epidemic in 1905 that temporarily reverted Mapandan to Mangaldan's jurisdiction, the municipality was re-established under American civil administration through Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith in 1909. No. 5, S-2024 Process Flow How an ordinance becomes law The legislative pipeline under the Local Government Code of 1991. 1 Filing A proposed ordinance is filed with the Sangguniang Bayan for consideration. 2 First Reading Initial reading and referral to the relevant committee for review. 3 Committee Hearing The committee holds hearings and deliberates on the proposal. 4 Committee Report Findings and recommendations are submitted back to the full council. 5 Second Reading Detailed floor discussion and debate on the proposed ordinance. 6 Third & Final Reading Final vote by the Sangguniang Bayan. 7 Mayor's Approval The Municipal Mayor reviews and approves the enacted ordinance. 8 Provincial Review Submitted to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Pangasinan for legal review under Sections 56 and 57 of R.A. 7160. 9 Posting & Effect The approved ordinance is posted publicly and takes effect across all 15 constituent barangays. Key Distinction Ordinance vs. Resolution Under the Local Government Code of 1991, the Sangguniang Bayan enacts two types of legislative measures: Ordinance A legislative measure that enacts a permanent rule or policy . Ordinances carry the force of law, create offices, levy taxes, or regulate conduct. They require three readings, publication, and the Mayor's approval (or passage by 2/3 override of a veto). Resolution A legislative measure that expresses the sentiment, intent, or opinion of the Sangguniang Bayan on a specific matter. Resolutions are used for internal housekeeping, requesting national action, or authorizing one-time transactions. They require only one reading and are not subject to publication.

title: About — BetterMapandan.org
description: About the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan, and the Better Mapandan civic transparency project.
body: About About Better Mapandan An independent civic transparency portal for the Municipality of Mapandan, Pangasinan. About Mapandan Ang bayan Kasaysayan Mapandan was created as an independent pueblo on December 28, 1887, through Director General No. 39. After a period of financial insolvency (1905–1908) when it was re-absorbed into Mangaldan, the town was re-established as an independent municipality in 1909 under Executive Order No. 10 by Governor General James F. Smith. The town was named for the abundance of fragrant pandan plants in the area. Heograpiya Mapandan is a third-class municipality in the province of Pangasinan, Philippines. It covers a land area of 32.92 km² and is composed of 15 barangays. The municipality is located in the western part of Pangasinan, bordered by the Lingayen Gulf to the north and the Agno River floodplain to the south. Population 38,228 PSA Census 2020 Land Area 32.92 km² MPDC Land Use Plan 2024 Barangay 15 DILG / Comelec Kasaysayan Ang Mapandan sa mga taon 1887–1909 From southern barrios of Mangaldan to an independent pueblo—and back again. Mapandan’s first two decades were defined by the courage of its founders, the fragility of a new town, and the determination to rise again. Basahin pa Before 1887: Southern barrios of Mangaldan Before Mapandan existed as an independent pueblo, the area belonged to Mangaldan. The future municipality consisted of southern communities including Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The movement toward establishing a separate town was initiated by ten local leaders: Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, Andres Bongato, Ambrosio Calimlim, Valeriano Tamondong, Tomas Aquino, Fulgencio Nato, Filomeno Sarmiento, Jose Lalas, and Florencio Datuin. December 28, 1887: Mapandan becomes a pueblo Mapandan was established as an independent pueblo through Direction General No. 39, Administration Civil No. 169-C, signed by Governor General Emilio Bravo. The new pueblo was initially composed of the southern barrios of Mangaldan: Payapay, Baloling, Apaya and Amanoaoac. The first town center: Torres The first center of the new pueblo was in what is now Barangay Torres. The area had abundant pandan plants and was associated with a church where Fr. Jose Torres served as parish priest. However, the location proved inconvenient—too close to the southern boundary and too far from communities to the north. The center was eventually transferred to an area that had previously been a sitio of Apaya. Much of the land in the new Poblacion was owned by the Aquino family. Leon Hilario Aquino encouraged settlement by subdividing land into uniform lots and making them available to families. 1903: The epidemic An epidemic severely affected Mapandan, causing major population depletion, residents leaving the town, declining municipal resources, and a financial crisis. The 1903 census recorded Mapandan’s population at 4,198. 1905–1908: Return to Mangaldan Because of the population and financial problems caused by the epidemic, Mapandan was temporarily returned to its mother municipality, Mangaldan. 1909: Restoration Mapandan was formally re-established as a municipality under Executive Order No. 10, signed by Governor General James F. Smith. 1910s–1940s After its restoration, Mapandan developed as a predominantly agricultural community. Farming remained central to the local economy, with rice becoming the municipality’s principal crop. The decades ahead would bring war, occupation, and the beginning of reconstruction. Basahin pa Agricultural foundations Rice became the municipality’s principal crop and livestock raising developed as an important secondary livelihood. The municipality’s current seal still reflects these agricultural foundations through its rice, cattle, chicken and hog imagery. 1940s: War, occupation and rebuilding The Second World War interrupted the development of communities across Pangasinan. In the postwar years, Mapandan’s communities entered a period of reconstruction and social and economic change. The decades following the war also brought changes in landholding, agriculture, education and local community organization. 1940s–1970s After the war, Mapandan’s communities began to take shape. New barangays were formed, land ownership changed hands, and the municipality entered a period of organized community development. Basahin pa Barangays begin taking shape Instead of only telling municipal history, the history of how Mapandan’s communities formed tells an equally important story. Sta. Maria — Formerly part of Luyan, developed from former hacienda land. Tenants gained opportunities to own the land they had been farming after the war. It became a separate barrio in 1965. Golden — Formerly Amanoaoac North, a sitio of Amanoaoac. Its name was associated with the Golden Distillery, which operated after liberation. Golden became a separate barangay in 1967. Torres — The first seat of Mapandan, which once contained several sitios that later developed into separate barangays. 1967–1973: Community development Golden was officially approved as a separate barangay in 1967. The community then underwent substantial development including road improvement, waterworks, school construction, sports facilities, cooperative organization, agricultural training, and sanitation programs. 1972 — Golden was recognized as a SEATO/PACD Model Village, receiving a national-level award presented in Malacañang on September 8, 1972. 1972–1973 — Coral became a barangay through Municipal Council Resolution No. 87 (May 4, 1972), Provincial Board Resolution No. 155 (August 10, 1972), and Proclamation No. 11 (April 25, 1973), followed by a special election for barangay officials on May 6, 1973. 1980s–2001 Modernization Mapandan’s population grew substantially, its services expanded, and infrastructure developed. The municipality moved from historical survival toward economic growth. Read more Population growth Mapandan’s population grew steadily through the second half of the 20th century: 20,094 in 1980, 25,622 in 1990, and 30,775 in 2000. Infrastructure and services The municipality expanded roads, schools, health facilities, and public services. Community organizations grew alongside the population. 2002–2024 From a new municipal classification to healthcare expansion and digital government—Mapandan enters the 21st century with growing services, cultural pride, and a more connected community. Read more 2002: A new municipal classification Mapandan was elevated to a third-class municipality. The municipality credits then-Mayor Jose Ferdinand Z. Calimlim Jr. with spearheading income and revenue-generation strategies that contributed to the municipality’s elevation. 2010s: Celebrating the Pandan heritage The Pandan Festival developed into an important annual celebration of Mapandan’s identity, culture and community. The 9th Pandan Festival was held alongside the town fiesta from March 11–19, 2018. 2017–2018: Early digital government efforts The municipal government began developing an online presence that made government information, public notices, disaster information and community announcements accessible through the web. 2022–2024: Expanding healthcare access National health infrastructure funding supported the development of the Mapandan Super Health Center. The 2022 General Appropriations Act included ₱6.5 million for the project. Its first phase was inaugurated on March 15, 2024, expanding access to laboratory, dental and primary healthcare services for residents of Mapandan and nearby communities. 2020s: Government services go digital Mapandan’s government information infrastructure increasingly incorporates digital channels, including information and access guidance for the national eGovPH platform. 2024: Mapandan today More than 130 years after its establishment as a pueblo, Mapandan is a 15-barangay municipality with a population of 38,228. Its history has been shaped by migration, agriculture, community organization, local government, cultural traditions and continuing investment in public services. ← 1 / 5 → Source: Mayor Karl Vega, “History of Mapandan” — YouTube Paglago ng Populasyon Ang Mapandan sa pamamagitan ng senso Populasyon ayon sa taon ng census Year Population 1903 4,198 1918 6,049 1939 7,286 1948 9,836 1960 13,065 1970 16,653 1980 20,094 1990 25,622 2000 30,775 2010 34,077 2020 38,058 2024 38,228 Source: Philippine Statistics Authority, Census of Population (1903–2024) About the Project Ano ang Better Mapandan? Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is part of the BetterGov.ph initiative to create open, accessible civic information websites for Philippine municipalities. Aming Misyon To make government information accessible, understandable, and actionable for every Mapandan resident. We believe that open data strengthens democracy and empowers communities to participate meaningfully in local governance. Kung Paano Ito Gumagana We compile publicly available government data — from COA audit reports, PSA census data, municipal disclosures, and provincial issuances — into a single, easy-to-navigate website. Every piece of information is sourced and attributed. Open Source The source code is publicly available. Developers can contribute, audit, and improve the platform. View on GitHub → Independent Better Mapandan is not an official government website. It is a community-run project that operates independently of the Local Government Unit. Pinapatakbo ng mga Boluntaryo Built and maintained entirely by volunteers. No government funding is used. Cost to the people of Mapandan: ₱0. Contribute Makilahok Better Mapandan thrives on community participation. Here's how you can help: Iulat ang Maliwang Impormasyon Spotted an error? Help us keep the data accurate by reporting mistakes. Report an error → Mag-contribute ng Code Developers can contribute features, fix bugs, or improve accessibility on GitHub. Fork on GitHub → I-verify ang Datos Help verify government information by cross-referencing with official sources. Submit verification → Ibahagi sa mga Residente Spread the word about Better Mapandan so more residents can access government information. Disclaimer Mahalagang Paunawa Better Mapandan is an independent community project and is not an official website of the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. Information presented on this site is compiled from publicly available government sources and community research. While we strive for accuracy, we cannot guarantee the completeness or timeliness of all data. For official government information, please visit mapandan.gov.ph or contact the municipal government directly.

Mga opisyal, badyet, ordinansa, at mga serbisyo para sa Bayan ng Mapandan — tinipon mula sa mga pampublikong talaan at inilagay sa iisang lugar, upang ang bawat residente ay makahanap ng kung ano ang ginagawa ng kanilang lokal na pamahalaan. Sakop nito ang 30.00 square kilometro, kung saan halos tatlo sa apat na bahagi ng lupain ay suportado ang agrikultura — pangunahin ang palain, kasama ang mais, hayop, at mga pan겻ang gulay. Ang pamahalaang bayan ay gumagana sa ilalim ng tagline “Kaakibat niyo ang Aktibo at Responsableng Liderato.” 01 Itinatag noong Dis. 28, 1887 Hiwalay sa Mangaldan bilang isang independenteng pueblo sa ilalim ni Heneral Gobernador Emilio Bravo, pinamunuan ng sampung lokal na lider kabilang si Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, at Andres Bongato. 02 Muling itinatag noong 1909 Isang matinding epidemya ang nagpilit sa pansamantalang pagsasama muli sa Mangaldan. Ang buong kasarinlan ay naibalik sa pamamagitan ng Executive Order Blg. 10 ni Heneral Gobernador James F. Smith. 03 Puso ng Agrikultura Humigit-kumulang 75% ng 30 km² ng munisipalidad ay inilaan para sa produksyon ng lowland crop, hayop, at pag-aalaga ng manok. Maikling Kasaysayan Ang Kwento ng Mapandan Mula sa bagong pueblo patungo sa isang lumalagong komunidad Itinatag noong Dis. 28, 1887 Mga Ugaling Katutubo Ang lugar ay kabilang sa Mangaldan bilang mga timog na barrio — Payapay, Baloling, Apaya, at Amanoaoac — pinangalanan para sa kasaganaan ng mabangong halamang pandan sa kapatagan ng Ilog Agno. Muling itinatag noong 1909 Pagkakatatag bilang Pueblo Itinatag bilang isang independenteng munisipalidad sa pamamagitan ng Director General Blg. 39, pinamunuan ng sampung lokal na lider kabilang si Antonio Morales, Sabino Prado, at Andres Bongato. Puso ng Agrikultura Pakikipagtalo at Pagbangon Isang matinding epidemya ang nagpilit sa pansamantalang pagsasama muli sa Mangaldan dahil sa krisis pinansyal. Ang buong kasarinlan ay naibalik noong 1909 sa ilalim ng Executive Order Blg. 10 ni Heneral Gobernador James F. Smith. Modernong Mapandan Isang 15-barangay na bayan na may 38,228 na residente, namumuhunan sa Super Health Center, Pandan Festival, at imprastraktura. Basahin ang buong kasaysayan at tuklasin ang mga makasaysayang larawan → Mga Kwento sa Likod ng mga Barangay 15 komunidad, 15 kasaysayan Bawat barangay ng Mapandan ay may sariling kwento ng pinagmulan, paglago, at buhay komunidad. Mga Pinagmulan at Talaang Kasaysayan Ang karamihan ng makasaysayang materyal ng Mapandan ay nagmula sa opisyal na website ng Munisipalidad ng Mapandan, kabilang ang Municipal Profile, Physical Characteristics, at mga indibidwal na kasaysayan ng barangay. Ang datos ng populasyon ay mula sa Philippine Statistics Authority. Ang mga milestone ng pag-unlad ay tumutukoy sa Philippine News Agency at Department of Budget and Management records. title: Accessibility Statement — BetterMapandan.org
description: Accessibility commitment and standards for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Support Accessibility Statement Our commitment to making government information accessible to all residents. Our commitment Better Mapandan is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for people with disabilities. We continually improve the user experience for everyone and apply the relevant accessibility standards. Conformance Status We aim to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at the AA level. These guidelines explain how to make web content more accessible for people with disabilities. Measures Taken We have implemented the following accessibility features across the site: Semantic HTML structure Skip-to-content navigation link Visible focus indicators Sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum) Keyboard-accessible navigation Screen-reader-friendly labels Descriptive link text Proper heading hierarchy Accessibility features Keyboard Navigation All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard. Use Tab to move between elements, Enter to activate links and buttons, and Escape to close overlays. Screen Readers The site uses semantic HTML, ARIA labels, and proper heading hierarchy to ensure screen readers can navigate the content effectively. Color & Contrast All text meets WCAG AA contrast requirements. Information is never conveyed through color alone — icons, labels, and text are always provided alongside color coding. Text Resizing The site uses relative units (rem, em) for text sizing. Users can resize text up to 200% without loss of content or functionality. Forms All form inputs are associated with labels. Error messages are descriptive and programmatically associated with the relevant input fields. Tables Data tables include proper header associations ( <th scope> ), captions where appropriate, and are responsive on mobile devices. Known limitations We are aware of the following accessibility limitations and are working to address them: PDF documents: Some linked government documents (COA reports, provincial issuances) may not be fully accessible. We provide HTML summaries where possible. Interactive maps: The Leaflet map is navigable via keyboard but may present challenges for screen reader users. We provide alternative text descriptions and a data table fallback. Third-party content: Embedded content from external government websites may not meet the same accessibility standards. Feedback We welcome your feedback on the accessibility of Better Mapandan. If you encounter accessibility barriers, please let us know: Report an Issue Use our reporting form to describe the accessibility issue, the page URL, and your browser/device information. Report accessibility issue → GitHub Issues Developers can file accessibility issues directly on our GitHub repository. Open GitHub issue →

title: Frequently Asked Questions — BetterMapandan.org
description: Common questions about government services, documents, and civic information for Mapandan, Pangasinan.
body: Support Frequently Asked Questions Answers to common questions about government services and civic information in Mapandan. General About Better Mapandan Is this an official government website? No. Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal built and maintained by volunteers. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Municipality of Mapandan or any government agency. For official information, visit mapandan.gov.ph . How is this project funded? Better Mapandan is entirely volunteer-run and uses no government funding. The cost to the people of Mapandan is ₱0. Hosting and domain costs are covered by the BetterGov.ph initiative. Where does the data come from? All data is compiled from publicly available government sources: COA audit reports, PSA census data, DILG disclosures, BLGF treasury data, provincial issuances, and municipal announcements. Every source is attributed on the page where the data appears. How do I report incorrect information? Visit our Report Incorrect Information page. Provide the page URL, the specific error, and the correct information if known. Our volunteers will review and update the data. Services Government services How do I get a birth certificate? Visit the Municipal Civil Registrar (MCR) at the 1st Floor, Main Municipal Building, Poblacion. Bring a valid ID and the required fee. Processing time is typically 3–5 working days. See the full requirements on the Birth Certificate service page . How do I apply for a business permit? Visit the Municipal Treasurer's Office (MTO) with your DTI/SEC registration, barangay clearance, and other required documents. New permits are processed in 3–5 working days. See the Business Permit service page for full details. How do I get a building permit? Apply through the Municipal Engineering Office (MEO). Building permits require a zoning clearance, architectural plans, and structural plans. Processing takes 10–15 working days. See the Building Permit service page . How do I request a barangay clearance? Visit your barangay hall with a valid ID. Barangay clearances are typically issued the same day. This is often a prerequisite for other government transactions. Data & Transparency Data questions What does "Placeholder" mean on data? Some data is marked as "Placeholder" when the exact figure is not yet available from official sources. We use reasonable estimates based on available data and clearly mark these so residents know the difference between verified and estimated figures. How often is the data updated? Each data section includes a "Last updated" timestamp. Major updates happen when new COA audit reports, PSA census data, or municipal financial disclosures become available. The site is continuously improved by volunteers. Can I download the data? Yes. The Statistics page includes CSV download options for chart data. The Transparency page provides links to source documents. All data is publicly available and free to reuse under open data principles. How can I verify the data myself? Every data section includes a source attribution and, where available, a link to the original document. You can cross-reference with official sources like the COA website, PSA, or the municipal government directly. Contact Still have questions? For government services Contact the relevant office directly. See the Government Directory for phone numbers and email addresses. For this website Report issues, suggest improvements, or contribute on GitHub . For data corrections, use the Report Incorrect Information form.

title: Privacy Policy — BetterMapandan.org
description: Privacy policy for the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal.
body: Legal Privacy Policy How we handle data on the Better Mapandan civic transparency portal. Overview Better Mapandan is an independent civic transparency portal. We collect minimal data and are committed to protecting your privacy. Information We Collect Automatically collected: When you visit Better Mapandan, our hosting provider (GitHub Pages) may collect standard web server logs including your IP address, browser type, referring URL, and pages visited. This is standard server operation and is not used to identify individual visitors. Search queries: The search functionality runs entirely in your browser. Your search queries are never sent to a server or stored. Language preference: If you use the language switcher (when available), your preference is stored locally in your browser and is never transmitted to us. How We Use Information We do not use, sell, or share personal information. Server logs are used only for maintaining the website and understanding usage patterns in aggregate. Cookies Better Mapandan does not use cookies. The language preference is stored using localStorage , which is a browser-only storage mechanism and is not transmitted to any server. Third-Party Services The site loads the following external resources: Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com) — for font loading Open-Meteo API (open-meteo.com) — for weather data (loaded only on the homepage) Leaflet / OpenStreetMap — for the interactive map (loaded only on the homepage) These services have their own privacy policies. We do not share any personal data with them. Data Sources All government data presented on this site is compiled from publicly available official sources. This data is already public and is presented here for informational purposes. Changes to This Policy This privacy policy may be updated from time to time. Changes will be posted on this page with an updated date. Contact For privacy-related inquiries, please open an issue on our GitHub repository or use the report form .

Statutory Batas sa Gastos sa Personal Section 325(a) of R.A. 7160 limits total personnel spending to 45% or 55% of total annual regular income depending on LGU classification.
